summary: All 16 units were re-reviewed in full and every numeric key, worked example and lesson figure was recomputed in Python (axial, thermal, torsion, power, flexure and I values, transformed sections, Q/I/t, shear flow, deflection, Mohr, rosette, combined loading, equivalent moments); all agree with the keys and tolerances. The round-1 fixes are confirmed: flexure-formula q010 is now correct (inverted T, flange at the bottom in tension at 19.7 MPa, stem tip in compression at 43.7 MPa, I = 5.674e6 mm^4, centroid 82.7 mm from the stem tip, with key, explanation and marking guide consistent); the web carries 91.8 percent of V (0.918 by numerical integration); and mohrs-circle q003 now correctly puts the highest point at (C, -R). Two minor issues remain, one of them a rendering defect introduced by the Q-formula edit. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: In the 'Distribution in a rectangle' text block the formula is stored as '$Q=\tfrac{b}{2}(h^2/4-y^2)$' with a single backslash in the JSON, so '\t' is parsed as a TAB character and the equation renders as 'Q=<tab>frac{b}{2}...' (garbled). The numbers in that paragraph (Q = 192 000 mm^3, tau = 3.52 MPa) are correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Escape the backslash in the JSON source (\\tfrac) or use \frac{b}{2}, then regenerate. Scan the same course for other single-backslash LaTeX commands starting with t, b, f, n or r.

issues.problem: The stem calls the section 'a cast-iron beam with an inverted T cross-section' and then asks 'which orientation (flange up or down) is preferable', so the stem already gives away the answer. It also gives no dimensions, while the explanation relies on the lesson's 120 x 20 flange and 20 x 100 web figures.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'a cast-iron beam with a T cross-section' (no 'inverted'), and either state the dimensions (flange 120 x 20 mm, web 20 x 100 mm, M = 3 kN m) or word the explanation as 'for the lesson section'. The key, explanation and marking guide are otherwise correct.
